object.alt: Object: Start: a body compared with Result: the whole body selected.
object.caption: Pick whole bodies, surfaces and curves. Use it to move, hide or analyze a whole part.

face.alt: Face: Start: a body compared with Result: one face selected.
face.caption: Pick individual faces. Faces are what supports, loads, holes and fillets act on.

edge.alt: Edge: Start: a body compared with Result: one edge selected.
edge.caption: Pick individual edges. Edges are what Fillet and Chamfer round and bevel.

vertex.alt: Vertex: Start: a body compared with Result: one corner selected.
vertex.caption: Pick individual corner points. Use it for measuring to a corner or editing freeform cage points.

rectangle.alt: Rectangle: Start: a body compared with Result: what the rectangle covered is selected.
rectangle.caption: Drag a rectangle to select everything inside it. Turn on Through to also take faces and edges hidden behind others.

lasso.alt: Lasso: Start: a body compared with Result: what the loop touched is selected.
lasso.caption: Draw around what you want to select. A lasso follows odd shapes better than a rectangle. Turn on Through to reach hidden faces too.

paint.alt: Paint: Start: a body compared with Result: the faces the stroke crossed.
paint.caption: Drag a stroke across the model: whatever the stroke crosses is selected. Shift adds, Ctrl removes.

group.alt: Group: A group adds a parent row; ungrouping keeps the objects.
group.caption: A group adds a parent row; ungrouping keeps the objects.

ungroup.alt: Ungroup: A group adds a parent row; ungrouping keeps the objects.
ungroup.caption: A group adds a parent row; ungrouping keeps the objects.

invert.alt: Invert: Start: a few faces selected compared with Result: all the other faces selected.
invert.caption: Select everything that is not selected. With nothing selected, Invert selects everything. Faces and edges invert within the bodies you picked from.

same-color.alt: Same Color: Start: one colored face selected compared with Result: all faces of the body with the same color and finish selected.
same-color.caption: Add every face that looks like a selected face. Colors are those set per face in the Appearance studio; faces that follow the body color match each other.

adjacent.alt: Adjacent: Start: one face selected compared with Result: the faces around it selected too.
adjacent.caption: Add the faces that share an edge with the selected faces. Hidden faces are skipped.

linked.alt: Linked: Start: one face selected compared with Result: all faces of that body selected.
linked.caption: Add every face of the body a selected face belongs to. Hidden faces are skipped.

through.alt: Through: Start: solid faces hide the inside compared with Result: hidden edges show through.
through.caption: See through faces to the geometry behind them. Use it to find internal holes and channels, or to pick geometry that is hidden behind a face.

gizmo.alt: Gizmo: Colored axes set the direction. Use the gizmo or enter exact values.
gizmo.caption: Colored axes set the direction. Use the gizmo or enter exact values.

point.alt: Point: A body compared with Points where you clicked.
point.caption: Place datum points: click a face, edge or empty space, and keep clicking to add more. In a sketch it starts the sketch Point tool instead.

axis.alt: Axis: A body compared with An axis along an edge.
axis.caption: Place a datum axis on an edge or face normal; empty space uses the work-plane normal. In a sketch this saves the gizmo axis as a sketch datum.

plane.alt: Plane: A body compared with A plane on its top face.
plane.caption: Place a datum plane on a face, plane or the work plane. In a sketch this saves the current datum plane.

create-sketch.alt: Create Sketch: Sketch geometry can be constrained and dimensioned.
create-sketch.caption: Sketch geometry can be constrained and dimensioned.

construction-plane.alt: Construction Plane: Start: a body compared with Result: a stack of offset planes.
construction-plane.caption: Make reference planes: offset (one or a whole stack), angled, midway, square to a curve or through three points. Sketch on the planes or use them as mirror, split and section references.

curve-from-data.alt: A real Curve from Data result: radius 12 mm, pitch 8 mm and five turns give 40 mm of axial rise.
curve-from-data.caption: A real Curve from Data result: radius 12 mm, pitch 8 mm and five turns give 40 mm of axial rise.

intersection-curve.alt: Intersection Curve: Start: a cylinder crossed by a plane compared with Result: the curve where they meet.
intersection-curve.caption: Make the curve where two planes, faces, surfaces or bodies cross, or the 3D curve shared by two flat curves on different planes. The curve is ordinary geometry: sweep along it, loft through it or trim with it.

project.alt: Project: Start: a curve above a body compared with Result: the curve lying on the face.
project.caption: Drop curves onto a surface, straight along a direction or by pulling to the nearest point. Projected curves can trim the surface or guide an emboss.

draw-on-surface.alt: Draw on Surface: Click points to draw across connected faces; the result can also split faces.
draw-on-surface.caption: Click points to draw across connected faces; the result can also split faces.

isocurves.alt: Isocurves: Start: a surface compared with Result: curves following its grid.
isocurves.caption: Pull curves of constant U or V out of a surface. Isocurves show how a surface flows and make good loft or sweep guides.

contour.alt: Contour: Start: a body compared with Result: evenly spaced slices.
contour.caption: Slice a body into evenly spaced section curves. Contours are handy for checking a shape's flow or for laser-cut layer models.

extract-edges.alt: Extract Edges: Start: pick an edge compared with Result: a curve copied from it.
extract-edges.caption: Copy selected edges as independent curves, joining edges that touch end to end. The copy is independent of the body: use it as a sweep path or a sketch reference.

fillet-chamfer.alt: Fillet / Chamfer joins two touching sheets and rounds their shared corner with a 6 mm radius.
fillet-chamfer.caption: Fillet / Chamfer joins two touching sheets and rounds their shared corner with a 6 mm radius.

rebuild-curve.alt: Rebuild Curve: Start: a lumpy curve with many points compared with Result: a smooth curve with few points.
rebuild-curve.caption: Redraw a curve with a chosen number of points. Fewer points make a smoother, fairer curve; more points follow the original closer.

points-along-curve.alt: Points Along Curve: A curve compared with Evenly spaced points.
points-along-curve.caption: Place points at equal distances along a curve; the curve's length is reported.

box.alt: Box: A point for a corner compared with A solid block.
box.caption: Drop a rectangular block into the model. Primitive sizes can be typed exactly or dragged with the on-screen arrows.

cylinder.alt: Cylinder: A center point compared with A solid cylinder.
cylinder.caption: Drop a round column into the model. Drag the radius and height arrows in the viewport for a quick size.

sphere.alt: Sphere: A center point compared with A solid sphere.
sphere.caption: Drop a ball into the model. Drag the radius arrow to size it by eye.

cone.alt: Cone: A base center point compared with A solid cone.
cone.caption: Drop a cone or truncated cone into the model. A top radius of 0 makes a sharp point; a larger value makes a frustum.

torus.alt: Torus: A center point compared with A solid ring.
torus.caption: Drop a ring shape into the model. The ring radius is measured to the center of the tube.

extrude.alt: Extrude: Start: a flat outline compared with Result: the outline extended.
extrude.caption: Give an outline depth by extending it in a straight line. A closed outline makes a solid. Use Cut to remove material from an existing body.

revolve.alt: Revolve: Start: an outline compared with Result: the outline spun around an axis.
revolve.caption: Spin an outline around an axis to create a round shape, like a knob or a bowl. A full turn is 360°. A closed outline can make a solid; an open curve makes a surface.

emboss.alt: Emboss: An outline over a face compared with The shape raised.
emboss.caption: Raise text or a sketched shape off a face, or engrave it into the body.

chamfer.alt: Chamfer: Start: select an edge compared with Result: a beveled edge.
chamfer.caption: Bevel a sharp edge on a solid or surface body with a flat angled face. Fillet rounds an edge; Chamfer cuts it back with a flat face. On a surface, pick an edge where two faces meet.

fillet.alt: Fillet: Start: select an edge compared with Result: a rounded edge.
fillet.caption: Round a sharp edge on a solid or surface body. A larger radius makes a broader curve. If it fails, try a smaller radius. On a surface, pick an edge where two faces meet; an open border edge is refused, so sew the surfaces first.

hole.alt: Hole: Start: select a face compared with Result: a hole in the face.
hole.caption: Drill a round hole into a face of a body. Choose Through All to cut the whole body, or enter a depth for a blind hole.

union.alt: Union: Start: two overlapping bodies compared with Result: one merged body.
union.caption: Merge bodies into one solid. The bodies must touch or overlap. Keep tool bodies leaves the originals in place.

subtract.alt: Subtract: Start: a body and a cutter (highlighted) compared with Result: the cutter's shape removed.
subtract.caption: Cut one body out of another. Only the first body is kept; the tool bodies are removed unless Keep tool bodies is on.

intersect.alt: Intersect: Start: two overlapping bodies compared with Result: only the shared volume.
intersect.caption: Keep only the volume that two bodies share. Everything outside the overlap is discarded. Use Subtract to remove the overlap instead.

linear.alt: Linear: Start: one object compared with Result: evenly spaced copies.
linear.caption: Repeat objects in a straight line at an even spacing. Add a second or third direction to make a grid or a block of copies.

circular.alt: Circular: Start: one object compared with Result: copies around the axis.
circular.caption: Repeat objects around an axis at an even angle. The copies are spread over the full 360° unless you set a smaller angle.

along-curve.alt: Along Curve: One object and a path compared with Copies following the path.
along-curve.caption: Repeat objects along a curve or edge chain.

fill.alt: Fill: A plate and one bump compared with A field of copies.
fill.caption: Fill a face or closed sketch with copies. Fill patterns suit vents, perforations and grips.

table.alt: Table: One object compared with Copies at the listed positions.
table.caption: Place copies at positions from a table. Positions can come from a sheet in the Data panel.

import-image.alt: Import Image: Pictures are references for tracing, placement and measurement.
import-image.caption: Pictures are references for tracing, placement and measurement.

edit-image.alt: Edit Image: Pictures are references for tracing, placement and measurement.
edit-image.caption: Pictures are references for tracing, placement and measurement.

set-scale.alt: Set Scale: Set Scale uses two picked points and their known real distance.
set-scale.caption: Set Scale uses two picked points and their known real distance.

ar-export.alt: AR Export: AR Export serves the phone page over your Wi-Fi; Stop Sharing ends that server.
ar-export.caption: AR Export serves the phone page over your Wi-Fi; Stop Sharing ends that server.

stop-sharing.alt: Stop Sharing: AR Export serves the phone page over your Wi-Fi; Stop Sharing ends that server.
stop-sharing.caption: AR Export serves the phone page over your Wi-Fi; Stop Sharing ends that server.

move.alt: Move: Start: a gap beside the post compared with Result: moved to touch the post.
move.caption: Slide objects to a new position. Type exact distances for precise placement. Snaps help line faces up. Hold Alt as you press an arrow or block to drag a copy and leave the original where it is.

rotate.alt: Rotate: Start: the part's orientation compared with Result: the part turned.
rotate.caption: Turn objects around an axis. Use it to lay a part flat for printing, or to turn it into the setup you need.

scale.alt: Scale: Start: the original size compared with Result: scaled.
scale.caption: Resize objects evenly, or stretch them along each axis. Uniform scaling changes every dimension. Per axis stretches along the world axes, so a part turned off-axis is sheared; curved faces become freeform surfaces.

mirror.alt: Mirror: Start: one side of a part compared with Result: the part and its reflection.
mirror.caption: Reflect objects across a plane to make a symmetric copy. Model half of a symmetric part, then mirror it, to keep both sides identical.

duplicate.alt: Duplicate: Copies are shown apart for clarity; position them as needed.
duplicate.caption: Copies are shown apart for clarity; position them as needed.

measure.alt: Measure: Start: select two faces compared with Result: the distance between them.
measure.caption: Read sizes, distances and angles between faces, edges, bodies or points. Select two parallel faces for a thickness; two edges for a distance or angle.

properties.alt: Properties: Start: a body compared with Result: center of mass marked.
properties.caption: Get volume, mass, center of mass and moments of inertia. Assign a material first so mass uses the real density.

section-analysis.alt: Section Analysis: Start: a block with an internal channel compared with Result: cut open to show the inside.
section-analysis.caption: Cut the model with a plane to see inside and read the section area. Move the plane to inspect wall thickness and hidden cavities.

materials.alt: Materials: Start: a body with no material compared with Result: material applied.
materials.caption: Choose the material so studies and renders use real values. Static studies use stiffness and strength, thermal studies use conductivity and heat capacity, frequencies use stiffness and density.

rib.alt: Rib: A bracket and a rib sketch compared with A rib joined to the body.
rib.caption: Add a reinforcing rib from a planar sketch to a solid body: the web between the sketch line and the body. The rib fills the corner between the line and the body, like a gusset. Reverse takes the other side of the line; Fixed height grows the line by a set height instead.

shell.alt: Shell: Start: select the face to open compared with Result: a hollow body.
shell.caption: Hollow out a solid, leaving walls of an even thickness. Keep the thickness smaller than the smallest feature, or the shell can fail.

draft.alt: Draft: Start: a part with straight walls compared with Result: walls with no draft in red.
draft.caption: Check faces for mold release in a pull direction. A few degrees of draft helps the part leave the mold. Straight walls show as red.

split-body.alt: Split Body: A body and a cutting plane compared with Two separate bodies.
split-body.caption: Cut a body into separate pieces with a plane, face or surface. Split Face divides a face without cutting the body.

direct-edit.alt: Direct Edit: Pick a face compared with The face pulled.
direct-edit.caption: Edit the geometry you already have, with no history needed: drag faces, holes and bosses with a gizmo. Works on imported parts too. Finish Editing returns to where you were.

extrude-surface.alt: Extrude: Start: a flat outline compared with Result: the outline extended.
extrude-surface.caption: Give an outline depth by extending it in a straight line. Surface mode makes walls without filling the ends.

revolve-surface.alt: Revolve: Start: an outline compared with Result: the outline spun around an axis.
revolve-surface.caption: Spin an outline around an axis to create a round shape, like a knob or a bowl. A full turn is 360°. A closed outline can make a solid; an open curve makes a surface.

sweep.alt: Surface Sweep using the scale table 0:1, 0.5:1.6, 1:0.7: the section grows at mid-path and narrows at the end.
sweep.caption: Surface Sweep using the scale table 0:1, 0.5:1.6, 1:0.7: the section grows at mid-path and narrows at the end.

pipe.alt: Pipe: Start: a path curve compared with Result: a tube along it.
pipe.caption: Make a round, optionally tapered tube along a path curve. Pipe needs only the path; Sweep needs a profile too.

loft.alt: Loft: Start: two separate outlines compared with Result: a transition between them.
loft.caption: Connect outlines to make a shape that changes size or shape along its length. A profile is one outline. Start with two profiles; guide rails are optional curves that control the sides.

boundary-surface.alt: Boundary Surface: Four boundary curves compared with A surface spanning them.
boundary-surface.caption: Fill or span a boundary of curves, sketches and surface edges. A flat loop gives a flat surface; curves across the inside shape the rest. Two separate surface edges are blended.

trim.alt: Trim: Start: a surface and a cutting plane compared with Result: the side you kept.
trim.caption: Cut a surface with a plane, another surface or a solid and keep the side you want. Untrim brings the cut-away part back.

split-surface.alt: Split Surface: Start: a surface and what cuts it compared with Result: the surface in several faces.
split-surface.caption: Divide a surface into faces along a plane, surface, solid, sketch or curve. Every piece is kept. Select a face of the split surface and press Delete to remove it. Choose Separate surfaces to color the pieces differently.

sew.alt: Sew with Merge combines the two coplanar halves into one face; the middle seam is gone.
sew.caption: Sew with Merge combines the two coplanar halves into one face; the middle seam is gone.

offset.alt: Offset: Start: a surface compared with Result: a parallel copy.
offset.caption: Create a parallel copy of a surface or face. Thicken makes a solid between a surface and its offset in one step.

thicken.alt: Thicken: A surface compared with A thin-walled solid.
thicken.caption: Give a surface thickness to make a solid.

unsew.alt: Unsew: Start: one closed body compared with Result: separate surfaces.
unsew.caption: Take a sewn shell, or just some of its faces, apart into separate surfaces. Sew joins them again; a closed result becomes a solid.

untrim.alt: Untrim: A face with a hole compared with The whole face.
untrim.caption: Undo a trim: restore the whole natural surface, or just fill the holes in a face.

extend.alt: Extend: A surface compared with The surface extended.
extend.caption: Grow a surface past one of its edges, continuing its shape.

reverse-normal.alt: Reverse Normal: The arrow changes which side faces out; the surface is not moved.
reverse-normal.caption: The arrow changes which side faces out; the surface is not moved.

enclosed-body.alt: Enclosed Body: A sheet over a plate compared with The space between, as a solid.
enclosed-body.caption: Make solids from the spaces enclosed by surfaces, planes and bodies.

flatten-refold.alt: Flatten / Refold: A curved surface compared with Its flat layout.
flatten-refold.caption: Flatten a surface and keep the layout, or wrap curves, sheets and solids back onto its source or another surface.

warp.alt: Warp: A straight bar compared with The bar twisted.
warp.caption: Bend, twist, taper or stretch bodies, surfaces, curves, forms or meshes along an axis.

convert-to-nurbs.alt: Convert to NURBS: Convert supported geometry into exact NURBS for further CAD work.
convert-to-nurbs.caption: Convert supported geometry into exact NURBS for further CAD work.

zebra-stripes.alt: Zebra Stripes: Start: a smooth shape compared with Result: reflection stripes.
zebra-stripes.caption: Show reflection stripes to judge how smooth a surface is. Smooth, continuous stripes mean a smooth surface. A kink or break shows a sudden change.

curvature-map.alt: Curvature Map: Start: a shape compared with Result: colored by curvature.
curvature-map.caption: Color surfaces by how sharply they bend. Flat areas stay blue; tight bends turn red. Smooth color changes mean a smooth surface.

draft-analysis.alt: Draft Analysis: Start: a part with straight walls compared with Result: walls with no draft in red.
draft-analysis.caption: Check faces for mold release in a pull direction. A few degrees of draft helps the part leave the mold. Straight walls show as red.

check-seam.alt: Check Seam: Check Seam samples compatible natural boundaries; it is not a global certificate.
check-seam.caption: Check Seam samples compatible natural boundaries; it is not a global certificate.

zebra-stripes-surface.alt: Zebra Stripes: Start: a smooth shape compared with Result: reflection stripes.
zebra-stripes-surface.caption: Show reflection stripes to judge how smooth a surface is. Smooth, continuous stripes mean a smooth surface. A kink or break shows a sudden change.

curvature-graph.alt: Curvature Graph: Start: a curve compared with Result: its curvature comb.
curvature-graph.caption: Show a comb of hairs along a curve to judge how smooth it is. An even, flowing comb means a fair curve; a sudden jump shows a kink.

plane-freeform.alt: Plane: A point compared with A flat grid of faces.
plane-freeform.caption: Start a form from a flat grid of faces to push, pull and sculpt. Use a plane for panels, wings and other thin shapes.

box-freeform.alt: Box: A point compared with A box cage.
box-freeform.caption: Start a form from a box cage that smooths into a rounded block. Most freeform shapes start as a box: pull its faces out into limbs and handles.

sphere-freeform.alt: Sphere: A point compared with A quad-ball cage.
sphere-freeform.caption: Start a form from a quad-ball: a sphere made of evenly sized four-sided faces. A quad-ball has no poles, so it smooths evenly everywhere.

cylinder-freeform.alt: Cylinder: A point compared with A cylinder cage.
cylinder-freeform.caption: Start a form from a cylinder cage, with or without caps. Leave the caps off for tubes and sleeves.

torus-freeform.alt: Torus: A point compared with A ring.
torus-freeform.caption: Start a form from a ring-shaped cage. Good for handles, grips and rings.

create-face.alt: Create Face: Clicked corners compared with A new face.
create-face.caption: Draw a face corner by corner.

loft-freeform.alt: Loft: Two curves compared with A form through them.
loft-freeform.caption: Build a form through two or more curves or sketches.

sweep-freeform.alt: Sweep: A profile and a path compared with A swept form.
sweep-freeform.caption: Carry a profile along a path to build a form (pipes, handles, limbs).

pipe-freeform.alt: Pipe: Start: a path curve compared with Result: a tube form along it.
pipe-freeform.caption: Make a round, taperable tube form along a path (limbs, tails, stems). The tube stays a freeform cage you can keep sculpting.

extrude-profile.alt: Extrude Profile: A profile compared with A form.
extrude-profile.caption: Pull a profile out into a form, optionally tapering.

revolve-freeform.alt: Revolve: A profile compared with A revolved form.
revolve-freeform.caption: Spin a profile around an axis into a form (vases, knobs, domes).

edit-freeform.alt: Edit Freeform: Start: a cage compared with Result: the cage reshaped.
edit-freeform.caption: Select vertices, edges or faces of the cage and move them with the manipulator. Move a few cage points at a time: the smooth surface follows.

extrude-freeform.alt: Extrude: Start: select a face compared with Result: the face pulled out.
extrude-freeform.caption: Extrude the selected faces (or open edges) out of the form. Extrude faces one ring at a time to build limbs with control.

slide.alt: Slide: Start: an edge loop compared with Result: the loop slid along.
slide.caption: Move the selected edge loop along its neighbouring edges without changing the shape much. Slide loops toward a corner to make the smooth surface sharper there.

subdivide.alt: Subdivide: A coarse cage compared with Finer faces.
subdivide.caption: Split the selected faces into smaller faces, or every face when none are selected. More faces give finer control but slower edits.

bevel.alt: Bevel: Start: a sharp edge compared with Result: a beveled edge.
bevel.caption: Bevel the selected cage edges: flat, or tight with support loops either side. Support loops keep the smooth surface tight to the edge.

delete.alt: Delete: Select the top face compared with An opening.
delete.caption: Delete the selected faces, edges or points. Fill holes caps the opening again.

split-face.alt: Split face: Start: a face compared with Result: the face in two.
split-face.caption: Cut a face in two between two selected corners. Split faces to route edge flow without adding a whole loop.

smooth.alt: Smooth: Start: a lumpy cage compared with Result: the points evened out.
smooth.caption: Relax the selected points toward their neighbours. Smoothing evens out spacing as well as bumps.

flatten.alt: Flatten: Start: a bumpy face compared with Result: the points pressed flat.
flatten.caption: Press the selected points onto a plane. Flatten the base of a form so it sits on a table.

fill-holes.alt: Fill holes: Start: a form with an open side compared with Result: the opening capped.
fill-holes.caption: Cap open borders of the form with faces. Closed forms convert to solids; open ones convert to surfaces.

thicken-freeform.alt: Thicken: Start: a thin sheet compared with Result: a sheet with thickness.
thicken-freeform.caption: Give the cage wall thickness. Thicken open forms before converting them to a solid.

insert-edge.alt: Insert Edge: Start: a coarse cage compared with Result: a new loop across it.
insert-edge.caption: Click an edge to add an edge loop across it. Add loops where you need more control, not everywhere.

inset.alt: Inset: Start: a face compared with Result: a smaller face with a ring around it.
inset.caption: Shrink the selected faces into smaller faces with a ring of new faces around them. Inset then Extrude makes buttons, vents and recesses.

select-loop.alt: Select Loop: Start: one edge compared with Result: the whole ring selected.
select-loop.caption: Select a whole edge loop or edge ring from the selected edge. Alt+L and Alt+R pick a loop or ring directly.

bridge.alt: Bridge: Two separate parts compared with A strip joining them.
bridge.caption: Join two selected groups of open edges with a strip of faces.

freeze.alt: Freeze: Half frozen compared with Only the free half moved.
freeze.caption: Lock the selected faces, edges or points so they cannot move (shown in blue).

align-to-curve.alt: Align to Curve: A cage and a curve compared with The cage on the curve.
align-to-curve.caption: Pull the selected points (or all) onto a curve.

smooth-surface.alt: Smooth surface: Start: the plain cage compared with Result: the smooth surface.
smooth-surface.caption: Switch between the smoothed surface and the plain cage faces. Edit with the cage visible and check the result smoothed.

weld.alt: Weld: Select the top face compared with The face collapsed to a point.
weld.caption: Pull the selection into one point: selected points weld together; edges and faces collapse.

crease.alt: Crease: A rounded form compared with The top edges sharp.
crease.caption: Make the selected cage edges sharp.

merge.alt: Merge: Start: two faces compared with Result: one face.
merge.caption: Join the selected faces into one, or remove the selected inner edges and join the faces either side. Merge to tidy edge flow after splitting.

unweld-edges.alt: Unweld edges: Start: one form compared with Result: split along the edges.
unweld-edges.caption: Split the form along the selected edges so each side can move on its own. Weld joins them again.

pull.alt: Pull: Start: a cage off its surface compared with Result: points on the surface.
pull.caption: Pull the selected points (or all) onto the smooth surface the cage produces. Pulling makes the cage points sit exactly on the shape you see.

flip-normals.alt: Flip normals: The arrow changes which side faces out; the surface is not moved.
flip-normals.caption: The arrow changes which side faces out; the surface is not moved.

mirror-and-weld.alt: Mirror and weld: Mirror and weld joins matching vertices along the mirror plane; this is a cage edit.
mirror-and-weld.caption: Mirror and weld joins matching vertices along the mirror plane; this is a cage edit.

check-quality.alt: Check Quality: Start: a form compared with Result: colored by curvature.
check-quality.caption: Mark poles, triangles and n-gons, see how stretched the quads are and how the curvature varies, or color the surface by its distance to a reference. Even curvature colors mean a smooth, well-spread cage.

check-cage.alt: Check Cage: Checks report geometry problems; review the report before repairing.
check-cage.caption: Checks report geometry problems; review the report before repairing.

convert-to-nurbs-freeform.alt: Convert to NURBS: A freeform cage compared with A smooth NURBS solid.
convert-to-nurbs-freeform.caption: Turn the selected form into exact NURBS surfaces or a solid for CAD operations.

convert-fewer-faces.alt: Convert fewer faces: Start: a form compared with Result: a lighter NURBS solid.
convert-fewer-faces.caption: Convert to NURBS with one fitted patch per irregular face instead of four: a lighter solid, a little less exact near poles. Lighter solids are quicker for booleans and fillets.

control-grid.alt: Control Grid: A grid of points compared with A surface through them.
control-grid.caption: Create a grid of control points to shape freely.

edit-points.alt: Edit Points: A flat patch compared with Points pulled up.
edit-points.caption: Drag NURBS control points, with soft influence on neighbours. Fewer points give smoother results. Shift-click adds points to the selection.

sculpt.alt: Sculpt: A flat patch compared with A sculpted bump.
sculpt.caption: Brush the surface: pull, push, move or smooth.

rebuild-surface.alt: Rebuild Surface: Start: a coarse patch compared with Result: the same shape, new grid.
rebuild-surface.caption: Redraw a surface as one patch with a chosen grid of control points. One clean patch is easier to edit and match than many small ones.

add-detail.alt: Add Detail: A coarse patch compared with The same shape, more points.
add-detail.caption: Insert knots so the selected curve or surface has more control points without changing its shape.

raise-degree.alt: Raise Degree: Start: a low-degree surface compared with Result: the same shape, more control.
raise-degree.caption: Increase the polynomial degree for smoother, more flexible surfaces without changing the shape. Degree 3 is usual; G2 matching needs degree 3 or more.

match-surface.alt: Match Surface: Start: two patches meeting at a kink compared with Result: a smooth joint.
match-surface.caption: Match compatible natural patch boundaries with G0, G1 or G2 continuity. Check Seam reports how well two boundaries meet.

edit-feature.alt: Edit Feature: A hole on the left compared with The hole moved.
edit-feature.caption: Pick a hole, slot, pocket, boss or fillet and move, copy, resize, retype or delete it. Holes can become counterbores, countersinks or modeled threads.

replace-face.alt: Replace Face: Start: a face and a sloped target compared with Result: the face on the target.
replace-face.caption: Make faces lie on another plane or face. The neighbouring faces stretch to stay connected.

match-face.alt: Match Face: Start: two different cylinders compared with Result: both the same radius.
match-face.caption: Give faces the plane, cylinder radius or cone angle of a source face. Handy for making imported bosses or holes match each other.

extend-trim-face.alt: Extend / Trim Face: Start: a face and a target plane compared with Result: the face moved to the target.
extend-trim-face.caption: Grow or shrink flat faces until they meet a target plane or face. Use it to make imported parts line up exactly.

split-face-direct-modeling.alt: A closed circle imprinted on the solid top creates a disc face without removing material.
split-face-direct-modeling.caption: A closed circle imprinted on the solid top creates a disc face without removing material.

edit-pattern.alt: Edit Pattern: Start: four holes in a row compared with Result: three holes, wider apart.
edit-pattern.caption: Change the spacing or count of a line, grid or circle of features, or drop one. Works on imported parts: the pattern is found from the geometry.

mirror-feature.alt: Mirror Feature: Start: one side of a part compared with Result: the part and its reflection.
mirror-feature.caption: Reflect objects across a plane to make a symmetric copy. Model half of a symmetric part, then mirror it, to keep both sides identical.

check-and-repair.alt: Check and Repair: Checks report geometry problems; review the report before repairing.
check-and-repair.caption: Checks report geometry problems; review the report before repairing.

fill-cap.alt: Fill / Cap: Start: a body with an open top compared with Result: the opening capped.
fill-cap.caption: Cap an open loop of edges with a flat face or smooth patch so the body closes. Use it after deleting faces or to close an imported shell.

merge-faces.alt: Merge Faces: Start: a face split by a seam compared with Result: one clean face.
merge-faces.caption: Join neighbouring faces on the same surface into one face, on a solid or a surface. Merging removes edges left over from imports and booleans.

finish-editing.alt: Finish Editing: Finish Editing leaves Direct Edit.
finish-editing.caption: Finish Editing leaves Direct Edit.

flange.alt: Flange: An open cross-section compared with A bent channel.
flange.caption: Make bent sheet metal from a sketch of its cross-section. Corners in the sketch become bends.

fold.alt: Fold: A flat outline with bend lines compared with A folded tray.
fold.caption: Fold a flat sketch of a sheet along its bend lines. The largest flat region stays put. Bends can run in any direction; keep holes and slots clear of the bend lines.

edge-flange.alt: Edge Flange: A flat sheet compared with The sheet with a flange.
edge-flange.caption: Add a flange along an edge of a sheet-metal body. The flange runs the whole length of the edge. Pick the thin end of the metal, not the top or bottom face.

flat-pattern.alt: Flat Pattern: A bent part compared with The flat blank with bend lines.
flat-pattern.caption: Unfold a bent body into its flat pattern with bend lines.

import-board-step.alt: Import board STEP: Import adds the supported geometry to the document; exchange files do not recreate Prism history.
import-board-step.caption: Import adds the supported geometry to the document; exchange files do not recreate Prism history.

rectangular-board.alt: Rectangular board: Start: an empty board area compared with Result: a board with mounting holes.
rectangular-board.caption: Make a rectangular circuit board with thickness, elevation and up to four mounting holes. Use Board from outline for any other shape.

board-from-outline.alt: Board from outline: Start: a closed outline compared with Result: a board of that shape.
board-from-outline.caption: Extrude a closed planar sketch, curve or face into a board. DXF outlines from ECAD tools import as sketches.

mounting-hole.alt: Mounting Hole: A board compared with A hole through it.
mounting-hole.caption: Cut a mechanical mounting hole through a flat board face.

component-envelope.alt: Component Envelope: Start: a board compared with Result: an envelope placed on it.
component-envelope.caption: Place a package envelope or mechanical keepout on the board, with top/bottom side and rotation. Envelopes let you check enclosure clearances before the real parts exist.

place-on-board.alt: Place on Board: The upright component is seated on the picked flat board face.
place-on-board.caption: The upright component is seated on the picked flat board face.

duplicate-ecad.alt: Duplicate: Copies are shown apart for clarity; position them as needed.
duplicate-ecad.caption: Copies are shown apart for clarity; position them as needed.

interference.alt: Interference: Start: two overlapping bodies compared with Result: the overlapping volume.
interference.caption: Find where solids overlap. Small overlaps can hide in fits; check mating parts after every change.

check-clearance.alt: Check Clearance: Compare the measured closest distance with the required clearance.
check-clearance.caption: Compare the measured closest distance with the required clearance.

section-view.alt: Section View: Start: a block with an internal channel compared with Result: cut open to show the inside.
section-view.caption: Cut the model with a plane to see inside and read the section area. Move the plane to inspect wall thickness and hidden cavities.

export-step-ecad.alt: Export STEP: Exact geometry for CAD exchange
export-step-ecad.caption: Exact geometry for CAD exchange

script-editor.alt: Script Editor: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.
script-editor.caption: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.

new-script.alt: New Script: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.
new-script.caption: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.

run-script.alt: Run Script...: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.
run-script.caption: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.

vs-code.alt: VS Code: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.
vs-code.caption: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.

pycharm.alt: PyCharm: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.
pycharm.caption: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.

scripts-folder.alt: Scripts Folder: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.
scripts-folder.caption: Python scripts use cadkit to create and inspect Prism geometry.

import-mold.alt: Import mold: Import adds the supported geometry to the document; exchange files do not recreate Prism history.
import-mold.caption: Import adds the supported geometry to the document; exchange files do not recreate Prism history.

cam-setup.alt: CAM setup: Start: the finished part compared with Result: stock around the part.
cam-setup.caption: Define the stock and the work zero that every operation uses. Leave a little extra stock on every side. Work zero should match how you will touch off on the machine.

select-setup.alt: Select setup: Start: several setups compared with Result: one setup active.
select-setup.caption: Switch between named stock and work-zero setups. Use one setup per way the part is held, such as top side and flipped.

tool-library.alt: Tool library: Start: one tool compared with Result: a library of saved tools.
tool-library.caption: Save named cutters with feeds and speeds for each material. Operations pick tools from this list, so spend the time here once.

design-check.alt: Design check: Start: a part with a thin wall compared with Result: the problem area highlighted.
design-check.caption: Find features a cutter cannot reach before you make toolpaths. Checks top-down access, tool reach and thin walls. Fix them in the model, or plan another setup.

profile.alt: Profile: Input: closed outline compared with Generated cutting moves.
profile.caption: Generate cutter passes around a closed outline to cut a part or its boundary. The preview shows cutting moves generated by Profile; rapid moves are omitted for clarity.

pocket.alt: Pocket: Input: closed outline compared with Generated cutting moves.
pocket.caption: Clear material inside a closed outline using successive cutter passes. The preview shows Pocket's generated cutting moves; nested outlines can leave islands.

adaptive.alt: Adaptive: Input: closed outline compared with Generated cutting moves.
adaptive.caption: Clear a pocket with an even cutter load, so you can cut deeper and faster. Curved, constant-engagement moves avoid slotting. Use a smaller stepover and deeper cut than for Pocket.

turning.alt: Turning: Input: half-section outline compared with Result: the turned part.
turning.caption: Face, rough and finish a round part on a lathe. The outline is turned about the part's axis, like Revolve. Put the axis on the sketch's edge.

drill.alt: Drill: Input: hole positions compared with Result: holes drilled.
drill.caption: Drill holes, with peck cycles for deep holes. Peck drilling retracts to clear chips; use it when depth is more than a few diameters.

face-subtractive.alt: Face: Input: raw stock compared with Generated cutting moves.
face-subtractive.caption: Skim the top of the stock flat with back-and-forth passes. Face first so later operations start from a clean, flat top.

image-carve.alt: Image Carve: Image Carve converts image brightness to cutting depth; the sketch shows a conceptual cross-section.
image-carve.caption: Image Carve converts image brightness to cutting depth; the sketch shows a conceptual cross-section.

3d-rough.alt: 3D Rough: Start: the 3D model compared with Result: stepped layers left for finishing.
3d-rough.caption: Remove most of the material in layers, leaving an allowance around the model. Roughing leaves steps on purpose; 3D Finish removes them.

3d-finish.alt: 3D Finish: Start: the roughed shape compared with Generated cutting moves.
3d-finish.caption: Follow the surface with parallel passes for a smooth finish. A smaller stepover leaves a smoother surface but takes longer.

constant-z-finish.alt: Constant-Z Finish: Constant-Z Finish follows steep walls with horizontal contour passes.
constant-z-finish.caption: Constant-Z Finish follows steep walls with horizontal contour passes.

playback.alt: Playback: Start: a finished path compared with Result: the tool moving along the path.
playback.caption: Animate a cutter or nozzle along its path. Watch for rapid moves through the part and unexpected plunges before you send the file to the machine.

operation-order.alt: Operation order: Start: operations in creation order compared with Result: operations in the chosen order.
operation-order.caption: Set the sequence the operations run in. Rough before finish, and use the same tool for operations next to each other to save tool changes.

stock-review.alt: Stock review: Start: untouched stock compared with Result: remaining stock colored.
stock-review.caption: Simulate material removal and see what is left. Red is the most material left. Check for gouges before posting.

setup-sheet.alt: Setup sheet: Start: operations compared with Result: a setup sheet listing them.
setup-sheet.caption: Review each operation and export a sheet for the machine operator. Include it with the G-code so the operator loads the right tools in the right order.

pass-view.alt: Pass view: Start: one finished pass compared with Result: all passes stacked by depth.
pass-view.caption: Step through the depth passes or print layers of a path. Use it to check depth of cut and where each layer begins.

post-g-code.alt: Post G-code: Post reviewed paths using the controller dialect. This abbreviated program is illustrative, not machine-ready code.
post-g-code.caption: Post reviewed paths using the controller dialect. This abbreviated program is illustrative, not machine-ready code.

place-on-bed.alt: Place on bed: Set a CAD solid down using the face you choose.
place-on-bed.caption: Set a CAD solid down using the face you choose.

fdm-check.alt: FDM check: Start: a part with an overhang compared with Result: the overhang highlighted.
fdm-check.caption: Find overhangs, thin walls and bed-contact problems before printing. Overhangs steeper than about 45° usually need supports. Try rotating the part first.

repair.alt: Repair: Start: a scan with stray fragments compared with Result: one clean, closed body.
repair.caption: Merge duplicate vertices, remove junk triangles, fix flipped normals and fill holes. Run Repair before Print Check or any slicing step; open or inverted meshes are the usual cause of failed prints.

mesh-quality.alt: Mesh Quality: Start: a mesh with hidden defects compared with Result: problem areas marked.
mesh-quality.caption: Find thin or stretched triangles, open and non-manifold edges and self-intersections. Highlights stay on screen after the command closes; use Clear Colors to remove them.

overhang-orientation.alt: Overhang & Orientation: Start: a part that needs a lot of support compared with Result: laid down with fewer supports.
overhang-orientation.caption: Find what needs supports and the best way to lay the part down. Fewer supports often means a rougher bed face; weigh surface finish against support removal.

wall-thickness.alt: Wall Thickness: Start: a part with thin and thick walls compared with Result: thin areas show in color.
wall-thickness.caption: Color the part by wall thickness to find walls that are too thin to print. The minimum printable wall depends on nozzle size or resin; check your printer's limit.

check-geometry.alt: Check geometry: Start: the model compared with Result: problem edges highlighted.
check-geometry.caption: Test the model for invalid geometry and open edges. Fix problems before you export; open edges can make slicers fail.

export-for-printing.alt: Export for printing: Start: the part compared with Result: the part ready for the slicer.
export-for-printing.caption: Write a print file for your slicer. 3MF keeps units and multiple bodies; STL is the widest supported.

tilt-part.alt: Tilt part: Start: the part's orientation compared with Result: the part turned.
tilt-part.caption: Turn objects around an axis. Use it to lay a part flat for printing, or to turn it into the setup you need.

hollow-body.alt: Hollow body: Start: select the face to open compared with Result: a hollow body.
hollow-body.caption: Hollow out a solid, leaving walls of an even thickness. Keep the thickness smaller than the smallest feature, or the shell can fail.

drain-vent-hole.alt: Drain / vent hole: Start: select a face compared with Result: a hole in the face.
drain-vent-hole.caption: Drill a round hole into a face of a body. Choose Through All to cut the whole body, or enter a depth for a blind hole.

resin-check.alt: Resin check: Start: an open cup compared with Result: the suction cup highlighted.
resin-check.caption: Find cups, trapped resin and thin features before printing. A cup that faces the build plate can trap resin. Tilt the part or add a drain hole, then recheck.

section.alt: Section: Start: a block with an internal channel compared with Result: cut open to show the inside.
section.caption: Cut the model with a plane to see inside and read the section area. Move the plane to inspect wall thickness and hidden cavities.

export-for-resin.alt: Export for resin: Start: the part compared with Result: the part ready for the slicer.
export-for-resin.caption: Write a print file for your slicer. 3MF keeps units and multiple bodies; STL is the widest supported.

bounding-box.alt: Bounding Box: Start: a part compared with Result: the box around it.
bounding-box.caption: Show the overall size box of the selection. Use it to check whether the part fits the stock or the build volume.

check-geometry-analyze.alt: Check Geometry: Start: the model compared with Result: problem edges highlighted.
check-geometry-analyze.caption: Test the model for invalid geometry and open edges. Fix problems before you export; open edges can make slicers fail.

clear-analysis.alt: Clear Analysis: Start: a colored result compared with Result: the normal model.
clear-analysis.caption: Remove result and analysis colors and show the normal model. Clearing only hides the colors; it does not delete the study.

make-drawing.alt: Make Drawing: Start: the 3D part compared with Result: flat views laid out on a sheet.
make-drawing.caption: Create an engineering drawing as PDF, SVG or DXF. Add dimensions, sections and a title block in the options before exporting.

solid-to-mesh.alt: Solid to Mesh: A solid compared with A triangle mesh.
solid-to-mesh.caption: Turn CAD bodies into triangle meshes.

import-point-cloud.alt: Import Point Cloud: Import adds the supported geometry to the document; exchange files do not recreate Prism history.
import-point-cloud.caption: Import adds the supported geometry to the document; exchange files do not recreate Prism history.

reconstruct-surface.alt: Reconstruct Surface: A point cloud compared with A mesh.
reconstruct-surface.caption: Build a mesh from the imported point cloud: clean up, estimate normals, set the detail and trim.

print-check.alt: Print Check: Check watertightness, build fit, support needs and weight before export.
print-check.caption: Check watertightness, build fit, support needs and weight before export.

select-region.alt: Select Region: A mesh compared with A region selected.
select-region.caption: Pick triangles on a mesh with smart patch, brush, rectangle or lasso, then delete and patch them, or extract them.

reduce.alt: Reduce: A dense mesh compared with Fewer triangles, same shape.
reduce.caption: Simplify a dense mesh while keeping its shape.

remesh.alt: Remesh: Start: uneven, stretched triangles compared with Result: even triangles.
remesh.caption: Rebuild a mesh with evenly sized triangles. Pick an edge length near the smallest detail you need to keep.

smooth-mesh.alt: Smooth: A noisy scan compared with A smooth mesh.
smooth-mesh.caption: Remove scanner noise without shrinking the part. Too much smoothing rounds off sharp edges.

split.alt: Split: Start: a part too big for the bed compared with Result: two pieces that fit.
split.caption: Cut a mesh with a plane and cap the halves. Cut where the pieces are easy to glue, and keep each half inside your build volume.

offset-mesh.alt: Offset: A mesh compared with The original and its offset.
offset-mesh.caption: Grow or shrink the surface of a mesh, for tolerances and clearances.

mesh-boolean.alt: Mesh Boolean: Start: two overlapping meshes compared with Result: one combined mesh.
mesh-boolean.caption: Combine two closed meshes: join, subtract or keep the overlap. Both meshes must be closed; run Repair first if you are told one is open.

clear-colors.alt: Clear Colors: Clear Colors removes mesh analysis coloring.
clear-colors.caption: Clear Colors removes mesh analysis coloring.

align.alt: Align: A tilted scan compared with The scan resting flat.
align.caption: Drop a mesh on the bed, lay a face flat, or best-fit it onto a CAD body.

section-sketch.alt: Section Sketch: A scan and a plane compared with A sketch of the section.
section-sketch.caption: Put a plane on the scan and get an editable sketch of fitted lines, arcs and circles.

segment-fit.alt: Segment & Fit: A scan compared with Exact faces.
segment-fit.caption: Find planes, cylinders, spheres and cones in a scan, read their sizes, and make them exact surfaces.

fit-surface-to-region.alt: Fit Surface to Region: A selected region compared with A surface fitted to it.
fit-surface-to-region.caption: Turn the selected region into a plane, cylinder, sphere, cone or smooth NURBS patch.

rebuild-from-scan.alt: Rebuild from Scan: Start: a scan mesh compared with Result: an exact solid.
rebuild-from-scan.caption: Automatic reverse engineering: fit all surface types, merge them, build faces and edge curves, sew, and report the deviation to the scan. Clean, aligned scans rebuild best; use Segment & Fit for manual control.

freeform-from-scan.alt: Freeform from Scan: A scan mesh compared with A quad cage around it.
freeform-from-scan.caption: Wrap an editable quad cage around the scan.

mesh-to-solid.alt: Mesh to Solid: A mesh compared with A solid of triangle faces.
mesh-to-solid.caption: Last resort: a CAD body with one face per triangle. Heavy and hard to edit; prefer Segment & Fit or Rebuild from Scan.

deviation.alt: Deviation: A scan compared with Colored by distance to the model.
deviation.caption: Compare a scan with its CAD model and show the error as colors.

new-study.alt: New Study: Start: a solid body compared with Result: the body is the study part.
new-study.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Start a static stress study on a solid body. A study needs at least one support and one load. Each study remembers its own supports, loads and material.

select-study.alt: Select Study: Start: several studies compared with Result: one study active.
select-study.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Switch to another saved static study. Each study keeps its own setup, so you can compare designs side by side.

materials-static.alt: Materials: Start: a body with no material compared with Result: material applied.
materials-static.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Choose the material so studies and renders use real values. Static studies use stiffness and strength, thermal studies use conductivity and heat capacity, frequencies use stiffness and density.

fixed-support.alt: Fixed Support: Study body compared with Selected support face.
fixed-support.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Keep selected faces from moving during a static study. The colored face illustrates the selection. A fixed support constrains all displacement directions.

roller-symmetry.alt: Roller / Symmetry: Study body compared with Selected roller face.
roller-symmetry.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Let selected faces slide in their plane but not move through it. Use it where a part rests on a smooth surface, or to model half of a symmetric part on its cut face.

fixed-directions.alt: Fixed Directions: Study body compared with Selected face, chosen directions locked.
fixed-directions.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Lock only the global directions you choose on selected faces. Unlocked directions stay free to move. Lock all three to get a Fixed Support.

force.alt: Force: Study body compared with Selected load face.
force.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Apply a force to selected faces of the study body. The colored face illustrates the selection; it is not a solved stress result.

pressure.alt: Pressure: Study body compared with Selected pressure face.
pressure.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Apply pressure to selected faces of the study body. The colored face illustrates the selection; pressure is applied over the selected area.

torque.alt: Torque: Study body compared with Selected torque face.
torque.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Apply a twisting moment to a flat face. The torque turns about the face's axis. Keep a support on the opposite end so the part cannot spin freely.

gravity.alt: Gravity: Study body compared with Whole body loaded by its weight.
gravity.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Include the part's own weight in the study. The weight comes from the material density, so assign a material first. It acts on the whole body.

create-mesh.alt: Create Mesh: Start: the smooth body compared with Result: the body divided into elements.
create-mesh.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Divide the body into small elements and look at the mesh before solving. Smaller elements give more accurate stress but take longer. The illustration shows a surface mesh only.

refinement.alt: Refinement: Start: a coarse mesh compared with Result: a finer mesh.
refinement.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Compare results on three meshes to see whether the mesh is fine enough. If the answer barely changes as the mesh gets finer, the result has converged.

run-study.alt: Run Study: Start: supports and loads set compared with Result: a solved stress field.
run-study.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Mesh the body if needed and solve the study. Colors illustrate a result; they are not a solved study. Check the mesh with Mesh refinement before trusting a number.

von-mises-stress.alt: von Mises Stress: Start: the solved model compared with Result: colored by stress.
von-mises-stress.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Color the model by equivalent stress. Red is high stress. Compare it with the yield strength, or use Factor of Safety.

displacement.alt: Displacement: Start: the undeformed model compared with Result: the deformed shape, colored by movement.
displacement.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Color the model by how far each point moves. The shape is exaggerated so small movements are visible. Check the legend for the real value.

safety-factor.alt: Safety Factor: Start: the solved model compared with Result: colored by safety margin.
safety-factor.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Show how far each point is from yielding. Yield strength divided by stress. Below 1 means the material yields; many designs aim for 1.5 or more.

probe.alt: Probe: Start: a colored result compared with Result: a value read at the clicked point.
probe.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Click the result to read the value at a point. Click near the highlighted areas first: peaks are usually at supports, holes and corners.

clear-results.alt: Clear Results: Start: a colored result compared with Result: the normal model.
clear-results.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Remove result and analysis colors and show the normal model. Clearing only hides the colors; it does not delete the study.

fatigue.alt: Fatigue: Start: the solved static stress compared with Result: colored by fatigue safety margin.
fatigue.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Estimate how many load cycles a part survives, and where it would crack first. An estimate from the material's ultimate strength, not test data. The static load is treated as the peak of a repeating cycle. Stress peaks at supports and point loads depend on the mesh.

generative-design.alt: Generative Design: Start: a solid block compared with Result: material removed where it is not needed.
generative-design.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Let the software remove the material that carries the least load. Keep out faces you need, such as bolt holes. The result is a suggestion to remodel, not a finished part.

save-face-selection.alt: Save face selection: Start: faces selected compared with Result: saved under a name.
save-face-selection.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Give the selected faces a name so you can reuse them. Use names such as bolt holes or contact face, then recall them in other studies.

recall-face-selection.alt: Recall face selection: Start: nothing selected compared with Result: the saved faces selected.
recall-face-selection.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Select a named group of faces again. Recalled faces are checked against the current body; faces that no longer exist are skipped.

saved-cae-setups.alt: Saved CAE setups: Start: a bare body compared with Result: supports and loads restored.
saved-cae-setups.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Run a saved case, with its supports and loads, again. Save a setup before you change the design so you can rerun it on the new shape.

export-results.alt: Export results: Start: a solved study compared with Result: values written to a file.
export-results.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Save nodal results and study details to a file. The file holds the values at each mesh node plus the study settings, for reports or other tools.

thermal-analysis.alt: Thermal Analysis: Start: a hot face selected compared with Result: temperature spread through the body.
thermal-analysis.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Find how heat flows through a solid between hot and cold faces. Steady shows the final state; transient shows how it changes over time. One uniform solid only.

materials-thermal.alt: Materials: Start: a body with no material compared with Result: material applied.
materials-thermal.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Choose the material so studies and renders use real values. Static studies use stiffness and strength, thermal studies use conductivity and heat capacity, frequencies use stiffness and density.

saved-setups.alt: Saved setups: Start: a bare body compared with Result: supports and loads restored.
saved-setups.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Run a saved case, with its supports and loads, again. Save a setup before you change the design so you can rerun it on the new shape.

recall-faces.alt: Recall faces: Start: nothing selected compared with Result: the saved faces selected.
recall-faces.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Select a named group of faces again. Recalled faces are checked against the current body; faces that no longer exist are skipped.

clear-results-thermal.alt: Clear Results: Start: a colored result compared with Result: the normal model.
clear-results-thermal.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Remove result and analysis colors and show the normal model. Clearing only hides the colors; it does not delete the study.

natural-frequencies.alt: Natural Frequencies: Start: a fixed support compared with Result: a vibration mode shape.
natural-frequencies.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Find the frequencies a part vibrates at, and the shape of each. The deformation amplitude is arbitrary. The shape matters, the size does not.

materials-dynamics.alt: Materials: Start: a body with no material compared with Result: material applied.
materials-dynamics.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Choose the material so studies and renders use real values. show-mode.alt: Show Mode: A mode shape illustrates a vibration pattern, not actual displacement amplitude.

motion-study.alt: Motion Study: Start: a link held out sideways compared with Result: the link swung down under its own weight.
motion-study.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Move any mechanism and read its motion, and with masses on, the forces it takes. Parts are rigid and joints and couplings are ideal: no flexing, backlash, tooth contact or contact between moving parts. Use a table for motion that comes from contact, such as a cam's lift.

materials-motion.alt: Materials: Start: a body with no material compared with Result: material applied.
materials-motion.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Choose the material so studies and renders use real values. spring-actuator.alt: Spring / Actuator: Connect points to add a spring, damper or actuator to a motion study. This is a setup diagram, not a simulated result.
spring-actuator.caption: Connect points to add a spring, damper or actuator to a motion study. This is a setup diagram, not a simulated result.

force-torque.alt: Force / Torque: Set force or torque direction and its constant, pulsed or alternating load. Arrows describe inputs, not solved motion.
force-torque.caption: Set force or torque direction and its constant, pulsed or alternating load. Arrows describe inputs, not solved motion.

clear-results-motion.alt: Clear Results: Start: a colored result compared with Result: the normal model.
clear-results-motion.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Remove result and analysis colors and show the normal model. Clearing only hides the colors; it does not delete the study.

load-from-motion.alt: Load from Motion: Use a calculated motion reaction as a load for a separate structural study.
load-from-motion.caption: Use a calculated motion reaction as a load for a separate structural study.

pipe-flow.alt: Pipe Flow: Start: a pipe compared with Result: pressure falling along the pipe.
pipe-flow.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. Estimate pressure drop and Reynolds number in a round pipe. A quick hand calculation, not 3D CFD. It does not model bends, valves or changes in size.

pipe-network.alt: Pipe Network: Pipe Network calculates steady node pressures and branch flows. Arrows are schematic, not calculated values.
pipe-network.caption: Pipe Network calculates steady node pressures and branch flows. Arrows are schematic, not calculated values.

flow-study.alt: Flow Study: Start: a body in the flow compared with Result: colors and streamlines of the flow.
flow-study.caption: Schematic help example; colors and deformation are illustrative, not results from a solved study. See flow around a body or through a duct, with drag and pressure drop. For Through, model the fluid itself as a solid. Trust the numbers for slow, smooth flow. Fast, turbulent flow is a picture, not a dependable number, and the results say so.

mate.alt: Mate: Start: two separate parts compared with Result: the faces mated.

exploded-view.alt: Exploded View: The assembled parts compared with The parts pulled apart.

rigid.alt: Rigid: Two parts compared with The parts joined.

revolute.alt: Revolute: Two parts compared with The parts joined.

slider.alt: Slider: Two parts compared with The parts joined.

cylindrical.alt: Cylindrical: Two parts compared with The parts joined.
cylindrical.caption: Turns about an axis and slides along it. Picking a body turns it into a part for you.

ball.alt: Ball: Two parts compared with The parts joined.
ball.caption: Pivots about a point. Picking a body turns it into a part for you.

planar.alt: Planar: Two parts compared with The parts joined.
planar.caption: Slides over a flat face in two directions. Picking a body turns it into a part for you.

couple.alt: Couple: Two parts compared with The parts joined.
couple.caption: Make one joint follow another at a ratio: gears, belts, chains, a rack, pulley, screw, lever or cable. Picking a body turns it into a part for you.

drive-joints.alt: Drive Joints: Start: the mechanism at rest compared with Result: a joint turned.
drive-joints.caption: Move the joints by hand to check the mechanism before simulating it. Check for clashes and limits here before running a Motion Study.

from-open-tab.alt: From open tab: Components connect the assembly to its part geometry.
from-open-tab.caption: Components connect the assembly to its part geometry.

create-mold.alt: Create Mold: A block and the part inside it compared with Two mold halves, shown exploded.
create-mold.caption: Cut a part out of a block, split the block in two and pull the halves apart. The part must sit completely inside the block. Choose the parting plane where the part is widest so it can be released.

draft-analysis-mold.alt: Draft analysis: Start: a part with straight walls compared with Result: walls with no draft in red.
draft-analysis-mold.caption: Check faces for mold release in a pull direction. A few degrees of draft helps the part leave the mold. Straight walls show as red.

section-analysis-mold.alt: Section analysis: Start: a block with an internal channel compared with Result: cut open to show the inside.
section-analysis-mold.caption: Cut the model with a plane to see inside and read the section area. Move the plane to inspect wall thickness and hidden cavities.

matte.alt: Matte: Finish comparison is schematic, not a measured render. Material assignment also supplies engineering data.
matte.caption: Finish comparison is schematic, not a measured render. Material assignment also supplies engineering data.

satin.alt: Satin: Finish comparison is schematic, not a measured render. Material assignment also supplies engineering data.
