find-assigned.alt: Find Assigned: Appearance and engineering material data are related but distinct; see the material controls.
find-assigned.caption: Appearance and engineering material data are related but distinct; see the material controls.

compare.alt: Compare: Compare stored material properties side by side; Clear Compare empties the table.
compare.caption: Compare stored material properties side by side; Clear Compare empties the table.

clear-compare.alt: Clear Compare: Compare stored material properties side by side; Clear Compare empties the table.
clear-compare.caption: Compare stored material properties side by side; Clear Compare empties the table.

done.alt: Done: Done closes the Materials tab.
done.caption: Done closes the Materials tab.

object-sketch.alt: Object: Start: a body compared with Result: the whole body selected.
object-sketch.caption: Pick whole bodies, surfaces and curves. Use it to move, hide or analyze a whole part.

face-sketch.alt: Face: Start: a body compared with Result: one face selected.
face-sketch.caption: Pick individual faces. Faces are what supports, loads, holes and fillets act on.

edge-sketch.alt: Edge: Start: a body compared with Result: one edge selected.
edge-sketch.caption: Pick individual edges. Edges are what Fillet and Chamfer round and bevel.

vertex-sketch.alt: Vertex: Start: a body compared with Result: one corner selected.
vertex-sketch.caption: Pick individual corner points. Use it for measuring to a corner or editing freeform cage points.

rectangle-sketch.alt: Rectangle: Start: a body compared with Result: what the rectangle covered is selected.
rectangle-sketch.caption: Drag a rectangle to select everything inside it. Turn on Through to also take faces and edges hidden behind others.

lasso-sketch.alt: Lasso: Start: a body compared with Result: what the loop touched is selected.
lasso-sketch.caption: Draw around what you want to select. A lasso follows odd shapes better than a rectangle. Turn on Through to reach hidden faces too.

paint-sketch.alt: Paint: Start: a body compared with Result: the faces the stroke crossed.
paint-sketch.caption: Drag a stroke across the model: whatever the stroke crosses is selected. Shift adds, Ctrl removes.

group-sketch.alt: Group: A group adds a parent row; ungrouping keeps the objects.
group-sketch.caption: A group adds a parent row; ungrouping keeps the objects.

ungroup-sketch.alt: Ungroup: A group adds a parent row; ungrouping keeps the objects.
ungroup-sketch.caption: A group adds a parent row; ungrouping keeps the objects.

invert-sketch.alt: Invert: Start: a few faces selected compared with Result: all the other faces selected.
invert-sketch.caption: Select everything that is not selected. With nothing selected, Invert selects everything. Faces and edges invert within the bodies you picked from.

same-color-sketch.alt: Same Color: Start: one colored face selected compared with Result: all faces of the body with the same color and finish selected.
same-color-sketch.caption: Add every face that looks like a selected face. Colors are those set per face in the Appearance studio; faces that follow the body color match each other.

adjacent-sketch.alt: Adjacent: Start: one face selected compared with Result: the faces around it selected too.
adjacent-sketch.caption: Add the faces that share an edge with the selected faces. Hidden faces are skipped.

linked-sketch.alt: Linked: Start: one face selected compared with Result: all faces of that body selected.
linked-sketch.caption: Add every face of the body a selected face belongs to. Hidden faces are skipped.

through-sketch.alt: Through: Start: solid faces hide the inside compared with Result: hidden edges show through.
through-sketch.caption: See through faces to the geometry behind them. Use it to find internal holes and channels, or to pick geometry that is hidden behind a face.

project-include.alt: Project / Include: A body above the sketch compared with Its outline in the sketch.
project-include.caption: Project edges or bodies onto the sketch, or intersect sketch curves with the active plane. Intersections with the active plane make loft rail anchors.

to-construction.alt: To construction: Start: a normal curve compared with Result: a dashed reference curve.
to-construction.caption: Turn the selected curves into reference (construction) geometry, or back into normal curves. Construction curves guide and constrain but are not part of profiles.

construction.alt: Construction: A normal curve compared with A dashed reference curve.
construction.caption: Construction mode (X): while it is pressed, new curves are reference geometry. Construction curves guide and constrain but are not part of profiles.

line.alt: Line: Clicked points compared with A chain of lines.
line.caption: Draw connected straight lines on the sketch plane, or lines from their midpoint. Horizontal and vertical lines are detected and constrained automatically. Choose Chain or Midpoint in the options bar.

rectangle-2.alt: Rectangle: First corner compared with A rectangle.
rectangle-2.caption: Draw a rectangle on the sketch plane. The sides keep horizontal and vertical constraints.

ellipse.alt: Ellipse: Center point compared with A circle or ellipse.
ellipse.caption: Draw a circle or an ellipse on the sketch plane. Circles and ellipses are closed outlines, ready to extrude.

arc.alt: Arc: Start and end points compared with An arc.
arc.caption: Draw a circular arc on the sketch plane. Options: 3-point, center, or tangent to the end of a line or arc.

spline.alt: Spline: Clicked points compared with A smooth curve.
spline.caption: Draw a smooth free-form curve through points, or pulled toward control points. Fewer points make a smoother curve. Turn on Curvature to check it.

polygon.alt: Polygon: Center point compared with A regular polygon.
polygon.caption: Draw a regular polygon on the sketch plane. Inscribed puts the corners on the guide circle; circumscribed makes the sides touch it.

slot.alt: Slot: Two arc centers compared with A slot.
slot.caption: Draw a slot: two arc centers, then the width.

text.alt: Text: An anchor point compared with Letter outlines.
text.caption: Type words and place them as closed outlines you can extrude or emboss.

trim-sketch.alt: Trim: Crossing lines compared with The middle part removed.
trim-sketch.caption: Cut a line, arc or circle back to the curves that cross it.

offset-sketch.alt: Offset: A curve compared with A parallel copy.
offset-sketch.caption: Copy a curve, or a whole connected chain, a set distance to one side. Offsetting a closed outline grows or shrinks the whole outline.

transform.alt: Transform: Colored axes set the direction. Use the gizmo or enter exact values.
transform.caption: Colored axes set the direction. Use the gizmo or enter exact values.

insert-point.alt: Insert Point: The curve gains an editing point; a line is divided into two segments.
insert-point.caption: The curve gains an editing point; a line is divided into two segments.

extend-sketch.alt: Extend: A line short of another compared with The line reaching it.
extend-sketch.caption: Lengthen a line or arc until it meets the next curve.

fillet-sketch.alt: Fillet: Sketch Fillet edits the corner between two lines in the sketch plane.
fillet-sketch.caption: Sketch Fillet edits the corner between two lines in the sketch plane.

chamfer-sketch.alt: Chamfer: Sketch Chamfer edits the corner between two lines in the sketch plane.
chamfer-sketch.caption: Sketch Chamfer edits the corner between two lines in the sketch plane.

mirror-sketch.alt: Mirror: Pick curves, finish selecting, then pick the mirror line. Live mode keeps both sides symmetric.
mirror-sketch.caption: Pick curves, finish selecting, then pick the mirror line. Live mode keeps both sides symmetric.

pattern.alt: Pattern: Start: one circle compared with Result: a row of copies.
pattern.caption: Repeat sketch curves along a direction or around a center.

horizontal.caption: Make a line horizontal, or line two points up horizontally. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

vertical.caption: Make a line vertical, or line two points up vertically. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

coincident.caption: Join two points, or put a point on a curve. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

parallel.caption: Make two lines parallel. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

perpendicular.caption: Make two lines meet at 90°. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

tangent.caption: Make a line and a circle or arc (or two circles) touch smoothly. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

equal.caption: Make two lines the same length, or two circles or arcs the same radius. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

midpoint.caption: Put a point at the middle of a line. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

concentric.caption: Give two circles or arcs the same center. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

collinear.caption: Put two lines on the same infinite line. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

symmetric.caption: Mirror two points across a line. Constraints show as small badges next to the geometry; delete one to free the shape.

fix.alt: Fix: Fix constrains the selected point or curve in the sketch.
fix.caption: Fix constrains the selected point or curve in the sketch.

dimension.alt: Dimension: A line compared with A driving dimension.
dimension.caption: Drive sizes with numbers: lengths, diameters, radii, distances and angles. Options: smart, horizontal or vertical.

curvature.alt: Curvature: Start: a curve compared with Result: its curvature comb.
curvature.caption: Show hairs along splines, ellipses and arcs that show how sharply they bend. An even, flowing comb means a fair curve; a sudden jump shows a kink.

grease-pencil.alt: Grease Pencil: A sketch compared with The sketch with a mark.
grease-pencil.caption: Draw freehand brainstorming marks on a sketch. Marks are saved annotations, separate from modeling curves, and do not snap or make profiles. Choose a color and a width of 1 to 12 pixels in the tool panel; yellow is the default.

eraser.alt: Eraser: Marks compared with One mark erased.
eraser.caption: Erase whole grease pencil marks. Undo restores an erase gesture. The eraser only touches grease pencil marks, not sketch geometry.

finish-sketch.alt: Finish Sketch: Finish Sketch keeps the sketch.
finish-sketch.caption: Finish Sketch keeps the sketch.

cancel.alt: Cancel: Cancel leaves sketch editing without keeping the sketch.
cancel.caption: Cancel leaves sketch editing without keeping the sketch.

zoom-extents.caption: Fit the model to the view.

set-home.alt: Set Home: Set Home stores your chosen model orientation.
set-home.caption: Set Home stores your chosen model orientation.

orthographic.alt: Orthographic: Start: perspective compared with Result: parallel edges stay parallel.
orthographic.caption: Show the model with parallel projection, so equal sizes look equal at any distance. Best for checking sizes and alignment. Standard views switch to orthographic automatically.

perspective.alt: Perspective: Start: orthographic compared with Result: edges converge with distance.
perspective.caption: Show the model as the eye sees it: far parts look smaller. Best for judging shape and presenting a part. Sizes on screen are no longer true.

single.alt: Single: Choose the viewport layout for the views you need.
single.caption: Choose the viewport layout for the views you need.

two-views.alt: Two Views: Choose the viewport layout for the views you need.

link-views.alt: Link Views: Linked views share panning and zooming.
link-views.caption: Linked views share panning and zooming.

shaded.alt: Shaded: With edge lines compared with Surfaces only.
shaded.caption: Show surfaces only, without edge lines.

shaded-edges.alt: Shaded + edges: Surfaces only compared with With edge lines.
shaded-edges.caption: Show surfaces with their edge lines.

wireframe.alt: Wireframe: Shaded compared with Edges only.
wireframe.caption: Show edges only.

x-ray.alt: X-ray: Start: solid faces hide the inside compared with Result: hidden edges show through.
x-ray.caption: See through faces to the geometry behind them. Use it to find internal holes and channels, or to pick geometry that is hidden behind a face.

hide.alt: Hide: Three bodies compared with The selected one hidden.
hide.caption: Hide the selected objects. Show All brings them back. Hidden objects are only hidden, not deleted.

isolate.alt: Isolate: Start: several bodies compared with Result: only the selected body.
isolate.caption: Hide everything except the selected objects, or show only the faces you selected. Hidden objects are only hidden, not deleted. With faces selected, the other faces of those bodies are hidden too; nothing in the document changes.

show-all.alt: Show All: Some objects hidden compared with Everything shown.
show-all.caption: Show every hidden object.

grid.alt: Grid: The grid is a drawing reference; showing it does not change the model.
grid.caption: The grid is a drawing reference; showing it does not change the model.

data-table.alt: Data Table: Use a named sheet as @sheet-name for supported points, positions or motion inputs.
data-table.caption: Use a named sheet as @sheet-name for supported points, positions or motion inputs.

zebra-stripes-view.alt: Zebra stripes: Start: a smooth shape compared with Result: reflection stripes.
zebra-stripes-view.caption: Show reflection stripes to judge how smooth a surface is. Smooth, continuous stripes mean a smooth surface. A kink or break shows a sudden change.

section-view-view.alt: Section View: Start: a block with an internal channel compared with Result: cut open to show the inside.
section-view-view.caption: Cut the model with a plane to see inside and read the section area. Move the plane to inspect wall thickness and hidden cavities.
